overview: This Senate resolution thanks the people who ran and protected the presidential inauguration on January 20, 2025, when Donald J. Trump was sworn in as the 47th President. It names the Joint Congressional Committee on Inaugural Ceremonies (the group of lawmakers that plans the swearing-in), the Architect of the Capitol (who maintains the Capitol building and grounds), the Senate's Sergeant at Arms and Secretary, police, emergency workers, and volunteers. It praises them for adapting when unusually cold weather forced some events to move indoors, and thanks their families for their support. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on February 13, 2025.
for: Supporters say the staff, officers, and volunteers who reworked major events on short notice and kept crowds safe deserve formal recognition from the Senate.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
